email.definition: A message sent electronically through the internet to another person or group.

memo.definition: A short written message used to share information within an organization.

report.definition: A document presenting information, findings, or progress on a subject.

proposal.definition: A written plan or suggestion presented for consideration.

invoice.definition: An itemized statement of money owed for goods shipped or services rendered.

contract.definition: An agreement setting out obligations between parties.

letter.definition: A written message addressed to a person or organization.

newsletter.definition: A regularly distributed publication sharing news with members, staff, customers, or another audience.

press-release.definition: An official statement sent to journalists to announce news or an event.

minutes.definition: Written notes recording what was discussed and decided at a meeting.

deadline.definition: The latest time by which something must be finished.

milestone.definition: An important stage or achievement in a project.

deliverable.definition: A specified item or result that a project is expected to produce and provide.

stakeholder.definition: A person or group affected by or interested in a project or organization.

benchmark.definition: A standard by which something can be measured or judged.

kpi.definition: A key performance indicator, meaning a measurable value used to track progress toward an important business or organizational objective.
kpi.exampleUsage: The team chose response time as one KPI.

roi.definition: A measure comparing the financial return from an investment with its cost.

strategy.definition: An elaborate and systematic plan of action.

objective.definition: A specific result that a person or organization aims to achieve.

initiative.definition: A new plan or action started to solve a problem or make progress.

teamwork.definition: Cooperative work done by a team (especially when it is effective).

brainstorm.definition: To generate and share ideas about a question or problem before selecting or evaluating them.

feedback.definition: Information about someone's work or performance that helps them improve.

review.definition: An examination of work, results, or plans to assess them.

delegation.definition: Giving another person responsibility and authority to complete a task.

coordination.definition: Organizing people and tasks so they work together effectively.

synergy.definition: An improved result achieved when people or organizations work together.

consensus.definition: Agreement in the judgment or opinion reached by a group as a whole.

alignment.definition: Agreement between people's goals, plans, or actions.

follow-up.definition: A later action, message, or meeting used to continue, check, or complete something discussed earlier.
follow-up.exampleUsage: She sent a follow-up email after the meeting.

touch-base.definition: To contact someone briefly to exchange information or discuss progress.

circle-back.definition: To return to a subject later for further discussion.

moving-forward.definition: A business expression meaning from this point onward or in future work.
moving-forward.exampleUsage: Moving forward, the team will use the updated schedule.

action-items.definition: Specific tasks that people agree to complete after a meeting or discussion.
action-items.exampleUsage: The meeting notes list three action items.

best-practice.definition: A method generally considered effective for a particular kind of work.

takeaway.definition: An important point to remember from a discussion or experience.

bottleneck.definition: A stage that slows down the progress of a process.

scalable.definition: Able to grow or handle more work without losing effectiveness.

leverage.definition: To use a resource or advantage to achieve a result.
